To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in children treated with GH, IGF-I, and IGFBPB-3 levels were found to exceed the 95th percentile of the reference range for age in 7.9 and 0.3% of the cases in the GHD group, respectively, and in 32.2% and 3.5% of the cases of the non-GHD group.

IGF-I, and to a lesser extent IGFBP- 3, are predictive of 6-month height velocity in both GHD and GH-sufficient children, and that the combination of these IGF parameters with maximum GH and height velocity at baseline provides a model which is more accurate in predicting 1st- year height velocity than maximum GH or height velocity alone.
the IGF-I/ IGFBP- 3 ratio is an independent predictor of height velocity and that, in both GHD and in non-GHD children and adolescents, IGF-I, and IGFBPs can exceed the normal ranges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relevance of IGF-I and IGFBP levels during childhood and adolescence, in particular with regard to the treatment of GH deficiency (GFD) or non-GHD children.
the monitoring of IGF parameters during childhood and their predictive value in the first year of GH treatment.
the relevance of parameters of the IGF system during long-term GH therapy in GHD and non GHD children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IGF-I, and IGFBPs, are not reliable markers of GH status, and that they do not provide any additional information for the optimization of GH treatment in children.
, for the individual patient, the IGF parameters can be useful for monitoring GH therapy.
the IGF parameters are of limited use for predicting 1-year growth, but they may be helpful for monitoring GH therapy and for detecting GH insensitivity in patients with GHD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IGF system is an important parameter to monitor in the GH-treated child and adolescent.
the IGF system is an important part of GH therapy and should not be overlooked in the future.
IGF-I, and especially IGFBP- 3, is an important parameter for the prediction of growth in children and adolescents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGF system is a useful tool to monitor GH treatment in children and adolescents with GHD and non GHD.
the IGF parameters should be used in combination with the GH dose to predict 1st-year response to GH treatment in both GHD and normal children and adolescents.
the IGF system should be considered in addition to maximum growth hormone in the prediction of growth during the first year of treatment.
